title: b.lane_presets allocated at catalog.odin:480 leaks on every new fail-fast rejection path (11 leaks confirmed)
evidence: core/catalog.odin:480 `b.lane_presets = make([dynamic]Lane_Preset, 0, 4, allocator)`; the new reject rows return before `cat.balance = b` is ever reached, e.g. line 488-489 `if lp.id == "" { return {"balance.json", "lane_presets", "preset id empty"} }`, line 516-517 `if len(b.lane_presets) == 0 { return {"balance.json", "lane_presets", "missing or empty (the emphasis dial needs positions)"} }`, lines 526-531 (duplicate id / duplicate weights) and 546-548 (default not found). `cat.balance = b` is only assigned at the very end of the balance block. `odin test core -debug` leak detector output: `+++ leak ... [catalog.odin:480:catalogs_load()]` reproduced exactly 11 times in two consecutive runs (11 = the 11 new bal_rows reject tests).
detail: The new dynamic allocation is never freed on the 11 new balance.json reject paths; the local `b` dies with the array. Error-path-only (production aborts on catalog failure), same class as the file's pre-existing parse-leaks (base: 5028 leaks), but this is a NEW leak site introduced by the diff.
recommended_fix: On each early return after the make, `delete(b.lane_presets)` before returning (or move the make after all validation and append rows directly).

title: check_reject_balance's file assertion is inverted vs sibling check_reject — accepts a rejection from ANY file, skipping the rule check
evidence: core/catalog_test.odin:218-220: `if cerr.file != "balance.json" { testing.expectf(t, cerr.file != "", "expected a balance.json rejection (rule %q), got %q %q", want_rule, cerr.file, cerr.rule); return }` — when the rejection comes from a DIFFERENT non-empty file, `cerr.file != ""` is true so the expectf passes and the test returns without ever checking the rule. The sibling helper asserts the file explicitly: `check_reject :: proc(t, pkt, dem, want_file, want_rule) { ... testing.expectf(t, cerr.file == want_file, "rejection file: got %q want %q", cerr.file, want_file) ... }` (catalog_test.odin:63-75).
detail: The new helper never asserts the rejection file is balance.json; a wrong-file rejection would silently pass. Unreachable today only because the other four fixtures are fixed-valid — a latent gap, inconsistent with the existing check_reject pattern.
recommended_fix: Mirror check_reject: assert `cerr.file == "balance.json"` unconditionally before the rule check, and drop the inverted branch.
